title: hosted-api-retry-sanitizer-and-stable-timeout-mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Critical work to stop repeated customer-visible 5xx spikes and long tail timeouts during tenant surges. This ticket consolidates investigation findings into a coordinated fix: sanitize retry behavior at the gateway, decouple tenant admission from kernel-level timeouts, and add targeted telemetry/guards to prevent retry amplification during escalations. Goal: restore steady-state request success and reduce P95/P99 latency regressions observed during high-concurrency bursts for Hosted customers.
reproduction_steps: Trigger a synthetic tenant surge using load-testing harness (100s tps of concurrent streaming requests with variable prompt lengths)
Use SDKs with default retry settings to simulate customer clients (exponential backoff with 3 retries)
Observe increased 502/504 responses from frontdoor and edge proxies followed by a wave of SDK retries that amplify load
Capture traces for a sample tenant: frontdoor -> edge-proxy -> runtime -> model-worker; note long queue times and streaming timeouts
investigation_notes: Root cause is multi-factor: upstream kernel slowpaths (long seq length batches) + insufficient admission control at edge + SDK retry policy mismatch with circuit-breakers
Observed KV cache eviction spikes correlate with sequence-length heavy requests which caused worker stalls and long tail latencies
Edge kept accepting requests while runtime threadpools hit saturation; lack of tenant-scoped backpressure allowed noisy tenants to starve others
Current retry semantics (client-side) lack idempotency checks leading to replay storms; server-side idempotency tokens are optionally present but inconsistently honored
Telemetry gaps: no single signal that combines tenant concurrency, worker queue depth, and recent 5xx rate to drive coordinated throttling
fix_plan: Implement a gateway-side 'retry sanitizer' that rewrites incoming retry headers and enforces max inflight-per-tenant caps before forwarding
Introduce a short-lived admission token per request that the runtime validates; if runtime is saturated it returns a well-defined 429 with Retry-After to avoid ambiguous 5xxs
Lower runtime long-poll timeout on streaming idle to avoid worker-thread starvation under pathological prompt patterns (configurable by model/route)
Add tenant-scoped leaky-bucket admission at edge and a fast-path for priority customers; ensure admission decisions are propagated to tracing
Backfill idempotency-first testing in SDKs and document recommended retry knobs in SDK defaults
Add a heuristic in scheduler to prefer shorter batches when queue depth exceeds a threshold to reduce single-request blocking
risks_and_tradeoffs: Returning 429 instead of opaque 5xx changes customer behavior; some customers rely on retries and may need guidance
Admission tokens add small latency and complexity to the control plane calls; will be beta-gated under feature flag
Heuristic batch shaping may slightly reduce throughput in exchange for tail latency improvements
SDK default changes could break poorly implemented client retry logic; will require staged rollout and clear migration docs
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flagged canary in staging (internal tenants) with telemetry dashboards showing inflight, 5xx rate, and retry amplification metric
Phase 1: Roll out gateway retry sanitizer to 5% of frontdoors and monitor errors/latency for 48 hours
Phase 2: Enable tenant admission tokens + edge leaky-bucket for non-critical traffic in a single region; observe degradation metrics
Phase 3: Gradual global rollout of 429-based backpressure and runtime timeout tuning with automatic rollback triggers (slo breaches > 5% and error increase)
Phase 4: SDK default guidance and communication to customers with opt-in SDK toggles before changing defaults
acceptance_criteria: P95 and P99 request latency for hosted streaming routes reduced by at least 30% during synthetic tenant surges compared to baseline
5xx rate attributable to runtime saturation drops by >= 70% for test tenants during surge tests
Retry amplification metric (ratio of total requests issued by clients to accepted requests) reduced to <1.2 under load
No customer-facing regressions introduced in dedicated/private paths (end-to-end tests pass)
New telemetry surfaces (combined tenant heatmap + inflight queue depth + recent 5xx) available in Console and used by rollout guardrails
testing_plan: Create targeted chaos tests that simulate KV eviction and long-sequence worker stalls
Run multi-tenant surge scenarios with live SDK clients and record per-tenant SLA impact
Unit tests for gateway retry sanitizer logic and idempotency header rewriting
Load tests for admission token path to measure added latency and control-plane load
Integration tests ensuring 429 + Retry-After path triggers correct client behavior (no infinite retries)
customer_communication: Draft customer-facing incident summary for active escalations with clear guidance: set SDK retry count to 1 and enable client-side jitter while we rollout fixes
Provide a Technical FAQ describing 429 vs 5xx semantics and recommended SDK settings
Offer targeted support sessions for top 10 affected customers to validate client settings and assist migration
Postmortem and long-form remediation note to be published internally and accepted into the public incident FAQ after approval
monitoring_and_alerts: New dashboard tile: combined tenant inflight + queue depth with heatmap by region
Rollback alert: after rollout, if global P99 latency increases > 10% and 5xx rate increases, auto-disable feature-flag
SLO check: track % of tenants experiencing >2x baseline tail latency; treat remediation if >1% tenants affected
postmortem_actions: Finalize and apply SDK guidance and ship a patched minor SDK release with opt-in safer retry defaults
Bake admission token validation into Dedicated/Private deployment docs for parity
Schedule a follow-up project to harden KV cache eviction behavior and expose eviction-sensitive metrics
Run a tabletop incident drill with oncall and support to validate new runbooks and escalation steps
